title: Boss: the integrity toolkit
summary: A webhook gate, a password-derived key store, a key ring from one secret, and tamper-evident records.

steps.title: The webhook gate
prompt: Write a program for a webhook gateway. The first input line is the shared secret (use its UTF-8 bytes as the HMAC key). Every following line is a delivery:

(the body is everything after the first space). For each delivery print `accept <body>` if the signature is a valid HMAC-SHA256 of the body's UTF-8 bytes, or `reject` otherwise, including when the signature is not valid hex. Compare tags with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.
steps.starter: // The first line is the secret; then one delivery per line until the end.

tests.name: a changed body and a swapped signature

hints: Split at `line.IndexOf(' ')`: the left part is the hex signature, the rest is the body.

steps.title: A self-describing password hash
prompt: Store password-derived values in one self-describing string, so the iteration count can be raised later without breaking old entries:
- `string HashPassword(string password, byte[] salt, int iterations)` builds it (real code passes a random 16-byte salt and 600,000 iterations; the tests pass fixed values and 1,000).

- `bool VerifyPassword(string password, string stored)` parses it, re-derives with the stored salt and iterations, and compares with `FixedTimeEquals`. Anything malformed (wrong prefix, wrong number of parts, a non-number, bad Base64) returns `false` rather than throwing.
starter: string HashPassword(string password, byte[] salt, int iterations)
solution: string HashPassword(string password, byte[] salt, int iterations)
byte[] hash = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, 32);
if (!int.TryParse(parts[1], out int iterations) || iterations < 1) return false;
byte[] actual = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, 32);
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoSalt = "dojo-salt-16byte"u8.ToArray();
var dojoStored = HashPassword("correct horse", dojoSalt, 1000);

Dojo.Eq("the stored format", "pbkdf2-sha256$1000$ZG9qby1zYWx0LTE2Ynl0ZQ==$" + Convert.ToBase64String(Convert.FromHexString("9a91c670f37ed09112419df342b8e88c9e191ae187942749ed1f1474deb0d74c")), dojoStored);
Dojo.Check("the right password verifies", VerifyPassword("correct horse", dojoStored), "rejected the right password");
Dojo.Check("a wrong password fails", !VerifyPassword("Correct horse", dojoStored), "accepted a wrong password");
Dojo.Check("a lowered iteration count fails", !VerifyPassword("correct horse", dojoStored.Replace("$1000$", "$999$")), "accepted a tampered iteration count");
Dojo.Check("an older entry with other parameters still verifies", VerifyPassword("pw", HashPassword("pw", new byte[16], 500)), "rejected a 500-iteration entry");
Dojo.Check("a wrong prefix fails", !VerifyPassword("correct horse", dojoStored.Replace("pbkdf2-sha256", "md5")), "accepted another scheme");
Dojo.Check("garbage fails without throwing", !VerifyPassword("x", "pbkdf2-sha256$abc$!!$??"), "accepted garbage");
Dojo.Check("bad Base64 fails without throwing", !VerifyPassword("x", "pbkdf2-sha256$1000$!!!$???"), "accepted bad Base64");
hints: `int.TryParse` for the count, and a try/catch around the Base64 decoding.

steps.title: A key ring from one secret
prompt: A service holds one 32-byte master secret and derives a separate key for each subsystem. Write a program that reads the master secret as hex on the first line, then one subsystem name per line, and prints for each:
<name> <first 8 bytes of its key, lowercase hex>
Each key is HKDF-SHA256 of the master with no salt, 32 bytes, info `"vault:" + name`. Printing a short fingerprint (never the whole key) is how you check two machines derived the same key.
steps.starter: // Line 1: master secret as hex. Then one name per line.
solution: byte[] key = HKDF.DeriveKey(HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, master, 32, null, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("vault:" + name));

tests.name: the same name twice gives the same key

steps.title: Tamper-evident records
prompt: Seal text records so any change is detected. The seal uses a MAC key derived from a master key, never the master key itself.

- `string Seal(byte[] master, string record)` returns `record + "." + tag`, where `tag` is the Base64url (no padding) of `HMACSHA256(macKey, UTF8(record))`, and `macKey = HKDF-SHA256(master, 32 bytes, no salt, info "seal-mac")`.

- `string? Open(byte[] master, string sealedRecord)` returns the record if the tag is valid, otherwise `null`. Records may themselves contain `.`, so split at the **last** dot. Compare with `FixedTimeEquals`, and return `null` (do not throw) for a missing dot or a tag that is not valid Base64url.
solution: byte[] MacKey(byte[] master) => HKDF.DeriveKey(HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, master, 32, null, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("seal-mac"));
byte[] Tag(byte[] master, string record) => HMACSHA256.HashData(MacKey(master), Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(record));
string Seal(byte[] master, string record) => record + "." + ToB64Url(Tag(master, record));
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoMaster = Enumerable.Range(0, 32).Select(i => (byte)i).ToArray();
var dojoMacKey = System.Security.Cryptography.HKDF.DeriveKey(System.Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, dojoMaster, 32, null, "seal-mac"u8.ToArray());
var dojoExpectedTag = Convert.ToBase64String(System.Security.Cryptography.HMACSHA256.HashData(dojoMacKey, "user=ada;role=user"u8.ToArray())).TrimEnd('=').Replace('+', '-').Replace('/', '_');
var dojoSealed = Seal(dojoMaster, "user=ada;role=user");
Dojo.Eq("Seal appends the Base64url tag", "user=ada;role=user." + dojoExpectedTag, dojoSealed);
Dojo.Eq("Open returns the record", "user=ada;role=user", Open(dojoMaster, dojoSealed));
Dojo.Eq("a changed record is rejected", null, Open(dojoMaster, dojoSealed.Replace("role=user", "role=admin")));
Dojo.Eq("another master key is rejected", null, Open(new byte[32], dojoSealed));
Dojo.Eq("records with dots work", "v1.2.3", Open(dojoMaster, Seal(dojoMaster, "v1.2.3")));
Dojo.Eq("no dot is rejected", null, Open(dojoMaster, "nodot"));
Dojo.Eq("a garbage tag is rejected", null, Open(dojoMaster, "x.!!!"));

require.message: Derives the MAC key with HKDF

hints: Write small helpers: `MacKey`, `Tag`, and the two Base64url conversions from module 1.
